familyCast.storyDescription: Twenty-nine. An AI-assisted coder and self-described 'slopling', 'slopfeeder', and 'AI code proompter' who steers a language model through legacy billing code and catches its confident Friday 4 p.m. lies. Torn between the invisible mastery of his craft (Ryle's knowing-how, Scott's metis, Naur's living theory) and the visible promotion ladder.

fictionalCounterparts.name: Odysseus & Telemachus (Homer's The Odyssey / Ulysses 1954 / The Odyssey 2026)
fictionalCounterparts.detail: Feigns madness at the plough (salting the Jira sprint board), sails past monsters of management, strings the great bow of the billing service, and seeks recognition from his father in the orchard.

fictionalCounterparts.name: Poppy Li (Charlotte Nicdao in Apple TV+'s Mythic Quest)
fictionalCounterparts.detail: Brilliant lead engineer offered the co-creative director chair by Ian Grimm; embodies the question of whether promotion changes a builder 'for better, or for worse'.

fictionalCounterparts.name: Richard Hendricks & Bertram Gilfoyle (Thomas Middleditch & Martin Starr in HBO's Silicon Valley)
fictionalCounterparts.detail: Richard is the craftsman forced into the CEO chair where his know-how poorly translates; Gilfoyle is the server-room craftsman who stays at the bench out of contempt for status.

familyCast.storyDescription: Son of a forklift driver; a master toolmaker at the Hendry works who took the foreman's desk at 34 because his father cried with pride that someone in the family had risen above being 'hands'. Never admitted he missed feeling the burr on the lathe. Now grafts apple trees ('the committee') in the backyard orchard. Seen through his son's guesses.

fictionalCounterparts.name: Laertes (Homer's The Odyssey, Book 24)
fictionalCounterparts.detail: Works alone in his orchard in an old jacket; recognizes Odysseus not by a royal title but when Odysseus names the exact trees they tended together (thirteen pear, ten apple, forty fig).

fictionalCounterparts.name: Parent–Child Recognition Arc (AMC's The Audacity)
fictionalCounterparts.detail: Inverts The Audacity's bruised family satire (where teenage daughter Jamison tries to see the real parent behind the tech title) into a mutual craft recognition between father and son.

familyCast.storyDescription: The warm, observant bridge between Odie and his father. She spots the leaked promotion news first, calls Lars into the kitchen at Beat 4, sings in the choir during Beat 62, and announces Odie's return to Ithaca at Beat 94.

fictionalCounterparts.name: Penelope & Anticlea (Homer's The Odyssey)
fictionalCounterparts.detail: Penelope's daily weaving and nightly unweaving at the loom is explicitly invoked at Beat 81 as the model for defending a sacred daily craft hour against the Suitors.

characters.storyRole: Engineering Manager ('Quick chat :)' in Conference Room Olympus)
characters.realCounterpart: Corporate Tech Engineering Director / Palamedes at Aulis
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Ian Grimm (Rob McElhenney) & David Brittlesbee (David Hornsby) in Mythic Quest; Palamedes & Agamemnon in the Trojan Cycle
characters.quote: "Team. Lead. Five reports, the Agentic Velocity squad, a real title. You'd be prompting the people who prompt the machines... It's a joke with equity."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Ian Grimm (Mythic Quest): "This is the opportunity. This is the elevator, except it's a car, and I'm trapped in it with you, alone, and you're in the driver's seat."
characters.description: Warm, harried, genuinely fond of her people, fluent in the ladder's language and half-aware of its absurdity. When Odie feigns madness at the sprint board, she pulls Palamedes' trick by dragging the production database into his furrow.

characters.storyRole: Smooth Political Colleague & Chief Suitor ('The Odysseus of the Open-Plan Office')
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Brad Bakshi (Danny Pudi in Mythic Quest); Odysseus in Ovid's Metamorphoses XIII / Sophocles' Ajax; Antinous (Lead Suitor in The Odyssey)
characters.quote: "Huge, man. Huge. Let me know if you need help with the people stuff." (Prompts the model to 'just fix it holistically' and deletes Québec.)
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Detienne & Vernant on polymetis: adaptive, room-reading cunning intelligence that wins the Judgment of Arms over steady craft.
characters.description: Starts the slow clap at Aulis, 'covers' Odie's 1-on-1s during sabbatical, tries and fails to string the bow of the billing service, and wins the armor if Odie declines without passing on his craft.

links.label: Characters in Mythic Quest — TV Tropes

characters.fictionalCounterpart: Nelson 'Big Head' Bighetti (Josh Brener in HBO's Silicon Valley); Eurymachus (Suitor in The Odyssey)
characters.quote: Has been 'about to ship' the same feature since spring; wins the Slack poll by voting for himself four times from different devices; renames the team 'Velocity Pantheon'.
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Graeber's critique played as slapstick: failing upward with the grace of a hot-air balloon.
characters.description: Cheerful colleague who has never finished a feature and has never once been in the room when one failed. Embodies the farce of Silicon Valley's Big Head when Odie stalls at the Call.

links.label: Big Head — Silicon Valley HBO Max

characters.storyRole: Junior Engineer & Apprentice (Keeper of the Living Theory)
characters.realCounterpart: Apprentice in Lave & Wenger's Legitimate Peripheral Participation
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Telemachus & Eumaeus (The Odyssey); Dana Bryant (Imani Hakim in Mythic Quest)
characters.quote: "oh. OH. ok that's actually the whole job isn't it." / "billing went down again, i caught it before the model did. felt the too-clean thing. thought of you."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Peder Naur (1985): The theory of a program lives in people, so the only way to save it is to grow it in another person.
characters.description: Doesn't clap at Aulis; sends 11 p.m. questions about the billing retry loop. When Odie shares the living theory rather than just the patch, she becomes the vessel through which the craft survives.

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Ferry Café Guide (Coined 'Vibe Coding'; Blesses & Dissects the Craft)
characters.realCounterpart: Andrej Karpathy (OpenAI Co-Founder, Former Tesla AI Director, Founder of Eureka Labs)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Hermes / Athena disguised as Mentor at the start of Telemachus's and Odysseus's voyages
characters.quote: "I named it vibe coding, you know. As a half-joke... Then you're not vibing. You're steering. Which is interesting!"
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Coined 'vibe coding' (Feb 2025); left director-level management at Tesla to return to hands-on coding and teaching.
characters.description: Meets Odie on the first night of the sabbatical at a ferry café table with a *vibes* sticker on his laptop, posing the central epistemological test: does the theory live in your head or in the model's weights?

characters.storyRole: New-Manager Onboarding Facilitator on the Island of Aiaia
characters.realCounterpart: David Graeber's 'Taskmaster' Middle-Management Onboarding / Corporate Offsite Industry
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Circe (Homer's The Odyssey Book 10, turning crewmen into swine); Gavin Belson's Guru in Silicon Valley
characters.quote: "We'll begin by unlearning the urge to do the work yourself." (New leads from Sales and Platform say 'let's take this offline' in a way that sounds like grunting.)
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: David Graeber, Bullshit Jobs (2018): 'taskmasters' and the 'spiritual violence' of performing a role you know is hollow.
characters.description: Presides over an Airbnb in a former bottling plant with a lanyard and little cups of framework. Defeated only if Odie eats Hermes' herb Moly — blocking one sacred, non-negotiable coding hour a day.

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Keeper of Brookes's Ledger (The Veteran Who Said Yes and Wrote Down the Cost)
characters.realCounterpart: Fred Brooks (1931–2022, IBM System/360 Manager, UNC CS Founder, Author of The Mythical Man-Month)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Nestor of Pylos / Tiresias (The Odyssey) — the elder who survived the campaign and kept the account
characters.quote: "People think the law is about schedules. It's really about theory. The understanding in people's heads doesn't pour into new hires like water."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Fred Brooks, The Mythical Man-Month: "The management question, therefore, is not whether to build a pilot system and throw it away. You will do that." / Brooks's Law: "Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later."
characters.description: Courteous, white-haired elder at a desk the size of an IBM mainframe on an island made of paper. Shows Odie the two columns of his ledger: what management bought vs. what it charged.

links.label: IEEE Spectrum: Frederick Brooks Jr. Obituary

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: The Siren of the Inbox Sea (Drifted into Management Without Choosing It)
characters.realCounterpart: Linus Torvalds (Creator of the Linux Kernel and Git)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: The Sirens (Homer's The Odyssey Book 12, singing from the rock in the glassy sea)
characters.quote: "It wasn't a promotion. Nobody offered. The mail just... rose. Turns out understanding people is its own craft. Nobody hands you the theory for that either."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Linus Torvalds (2020): "I read email, I write email, I do no coding at all any more." (Plus his 2018 sabbatical to learn empathy on the kernel mailing list.)
characters.description: Sits on a rock in a cardigan with a laptop surrounded by 312 unread messages singing *Quick sync? Can you weigh in? Looping you in.*

links.label: Slashdot: Linus Torvalds 'I Do No Coding Any More'

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Co-Keeper of Bell Works Garden (Protected by the Institutional Umbrella)
characters.realCounterpart: Ken Thompson (Bell Labs Co-Creator of Unix & B; Google Distinguished Engineer & Co-Creator of Go)
characters.quote: "The good ones don't want to hold [the umbrella] at all. That's why it works. The trouble is, a ladder can't see the umbrella."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Ken Thompson on Bell Labs management (Wired, 1995): "just an umbrella, not really a focus of power."
characters.description: Hunched over a terminal in an ivy-draped brick laboratory, writing something small and perfect that will outlive everyone there.

links.label: ACM Turing Award Profile: Ken Thompson
Wired (1995): Ken Thompson at Bell Labs

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Co-Keeper of Bell Works Garden (Play as the Work Itself)
characters.realCounterpart: Claude Shannon (1916–2001, Father of Information Theory at Bell Labs & MIT; Built Theseus the Mouse)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: The Lotus-Eaters / Daedalus the Master Tinkerer
characters.quote: "The mouse is called Theseus. He knows the maze because he's walked it. You can't download walking it... The lotus here is just fun. Fun is the most dangerous thing there is."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Built Theseus (1950), rode a unicycle while juggling down Bell Labs corridors, and kept his craft alive through play.
characters.description: Rides past on a unicycle juggling three balls while his relay-operated mechanical mouse solves a maze on the lawn. Staying too long with him costs two island turns.

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: The Oracle in the GPU Cave (The Shaman-Leader Who Became CEO Anyway)
characters.realCounterpart: Ilya Sutskever (Co-Founder & Former Chief Scientist of OpenAI; CEO of Safe Superintelligence Inc.)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Pythia / The Oracle at Delphi; Gavin Belson (Matt Ross in Silicon Valley); Ian Grimm (Mythic Quest)
characters.quote: "WHICH PART OF YOU IS THE PART THAT KNOWS? ... Someone must keep the cave open. If I don't, someone who feels nothing will. That is the bargain."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Reported OpenAI chant: "Feel the AGI!" — and in July 2025 stepped into the CEO role at Safe Superintelligence ($32B valuation).
characters.description: Presides over a circle of researchers in a cave lit by GPU fans. His deep scientific charisma turned him into a spiritual leader, and the charisma pulled him back into the top job.

links.label: CNBC: Ilya Sutskever Is CEO of Safe Superintelligence

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Sun of the Flat Island at Vane (No Managers, Yet Everyone Bows)
characters.realCounterpart: Gabe Newell (Co-Founder & President of Valve Corporation)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Aeolus, Keeper of the Winds on the Floating Island of Aeolia (The Odyssey Book 10)
characters.quote: "Could work. Could also mean the power's still there and nobody's allowed to say where. Flat isn't the same as free. You'd have to be honest about the bowing."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Valve Handbook for New Employees (2012): "Of all the people at this company who aren't your boss, Gabe is the MOST not your boss."
characters.description: Very relaxed, very kind, munching a snack at the center of Vane while every rolling desk and decision gently curves toward him like planets around the sun.

links.label: BBC News: Valve's Manager-Free Flat Structure
Game Developer: Gabe Newell on Flat Structure

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Master of the Exile Workshop at Sharp Labs (Walked Away from Metta)
characters.realCounterpart: John Carmack (Co-Founder of id Software, Lead Programmer of Doom/Quake, Former Oculus CTO at Meta, Founder of Keen Technologies)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Philoctetes on Lemnos / Hephaestus at his Forge; Bertram Gilfoyle (Martin Starr in Silicon Valley)
characters.quote: "The work's better. The days are mine. Nobody schedules me into a meeting about the meeting... It's also just me and the problem. Most nights."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: John Carmack's December 2022 Meta resignation note: "This is the end of my decade in VR." / "We have a ridiculous amount of people and resources, but we constantly self-sabotage and squander effort." / "wearied of the fight."
characters.description: Works alone in a shed on a cold coast with an oscilloscope, a whiteboard, and one coffee mug. Shows both the pure freedom and the sharp loneliness of walking away from the big ship.

links.label: Daring Fireball: John Carmack's Full Resignation Letter
D Magazine (2025): Conversation with John Carmack at Keen Technologies

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Keeper of the Golden Charter Room at DeepMound (Rewrote His Own Role)
characters.realCounterpart: Sir Demis Hassabis (Elixir Studios Founder, UCL Neuroscience PhD, 2024 Nobel Laureate, Google DeepMind Chairman & Alphabet Chief Scientist, Isomorphic Labs CEO)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Calypso on the Golden Island of Ogygia (The Odyssey Book 5 — the golden cage)
characters.quote: "A charter is a tool, not a home. Remember who pays for it. Somebody always picks up what you put down. Leverage means you can refuse. It doesn't mean refusing is free."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Stepped back from games CEO to UCL PhD student (2005), and in August 2026 stepped from DeepMind CEO to Chairman to focus on AGI research and science.
characters.description: His golden room opens only if Odie's Leverage >= 5. Embodies the third path of redesigning one's own job description, while honestly framing its costs on colleagues and markets.

links.label: Academy of Achievement: Demis Hassabis Ph.D.
Google Blog: Next Chapter of AI Momentum

characters.category: Voyage Guides & Thinly Veiled Tech Pioneers
characters.storyRole: Master of Knuthe's Cave (Reached by a Ladder That Goes Down)
characters.realCounterpart: Donald Ervin Knuth (Author of The Art of Computer Programming, Creator of TeX & Literate Programming, Stanford Professor Emeritus)
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Proteus (The Old Man of the Sea) / Oracle of Trophonius in his subterranean cave
characters.quote: "Most people climb to see more. I go down to see better. It's slower. Nobody gives you a title for it. They give you a cave."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Donald Knuth (on giving up email in 1990): Email is for people whose role is to be "on top of things," whereas his role is to be "on the bottom of things."
characters.description: Works by lamplight at the bottom of a downward ladder with no inbox at all. Helps Odie trace a billing bug by hand for nine hours and urges him to grow the living theory in another person.

links.label: Cal Newport: Why Donald Knuth Quit Email ('Bottom of Things')

characters.storyName: Mau Piailug & The Elders of the Road
characters.storyRole: Master Navigator of Satawal & The Masters Who Rise by Going Deeper
characters.realCounterpart: Pius 'Mau' Piailug (1932–2010, Micronesian Master Navigator of the Weriyeng School on Satawal); Compagnons du Devoir; Japan's Living National Treasures; Ise Grand Shrine Carpenters
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Tiresias & The Phaeacian Mariners who carry Odysseus home across the sea
characters.quote: Portrayed with quiet reverence and zero comedy: "The ladder he climbed had no rungs anyone could see from an office. It went across the ocean and down through generations."
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Ise Grand Shrine (Smithsonian): "preserves the past by refreshing the people." Mau Piailug guided the Hōkūleʻa canoe from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti in 1976 without instruments.
characters.description: Where the Road of Older Ladders meets the sea, all satire stops. Mau Piailug's choice to share sacred wayfinding knowledge outside Satawal frames mastery as a consequential lineage of teaching.

links.label: JSTOR Daily: Pius 'Mau' Piailug, Master Navigator of Micronesia

characters.storyName: Peder Naur, Gilbert Ryle & James C. Scott
characters.storyRole: The Epistemological Triad Underneath the Odyssey
characters.realCounterpart: Peter Naur (2005 Turing Award, 'Programming as Theory Building'), Gilbert Ryle ('The Concept of Mind'), James C. Scott ('Seeing Like a State')
characters.quote: Ryle's knowing-how vs. knowing-that; Naur's living theory in the programmer's head; Scott's metis vs. the single eye of state/corporate legibility.
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Peter Naur (1985), Programming as Theory Building: A program's substance is the living theory held by its practitioners, which decays when no longer practiced.
characters.description: The three thinkers who give Odie the words for why turning down a promotion is not a lack of ambition, and why a dashboard cannot measure a craft.

links.label: Peter Naur (1985): Programming as Theory Building (PDF)

characters.storyRole: The Silent Craftsman-Warrior in the Conference Hotel Underworld
characters.realCounterpart: Every Burned-Out Senior Engineer Passed Over for a Smooth Talker
characters.fictionalCounterpart: Telamonian Ajax (Homer's The Odyssey Book 11 & Sophocles' Ajax); C.W. Longbottom (F. Murray Abraham in Mythic Quest)
characters.quote: *He says nothing.* Only the tools in his hands shift, the way a craftsman's hands shift when someone talks about the work instead of doing it.
characters.verifiedSourceQuote: Sophocles, Ajax: "Let a man nobly live or nobly die." / Odysseus pitying Ajax: "We are dim shapes, no more, and weightless shadows."
characters.description: Stands apart in the grey-carpeted conference hotel Underworld holding workman's tools. Refuses to speak to anyone on the ladder. In Beat 74, Odie sees an alternate vision where Ajax goes home to the forge, takes apprentices, and lives.

links.label: Ancient World Magazine: The Suicide of Ajax

places.storyName: Open-Plan Office & Conference Room 'Olympus' ('The Beach at Aulis')
places.realPlace: Modern Tech Office in Atlanta, GA / Georgia Tech CODA & Tech Square + Bay of Aulis (Boeotia, Greece)
places.fictionalPlace: Mythic Quest Studios Bullpen (Harrison & Sons Textiles Building) / Pied Piper Hacker Hostel / Port of Aulis (Iphigenia at Aulis)
places.description: At dusk, one monitor glows with a chat window full of billing code. On Friday at 10 a.m., Dana books the glass-walled conference room 'Olympus' with two HR people and a bowl of sad clementines. Outside, colleagues clap like the assembled Greeks pushing a reluctant captain onto the ship to Troy.

places.realPlace: 910 Taft Ave NE, Atlanta, GA (Midtown Atlanta Coder's Apartment)
places.fictionalPlace: Telemachus's Chamber in Ithaca before the Journey
places.description: Where Odie lies awake turning over Ryle and Naur at 1 a.m. before inspecting the three tokens on his desk (Prompt Journal, Brass Calipers, Offer Letter) and spending forty invisible minutes teaching Ines the theory of the billing retry loop.

places.description: A ferry café where biographies read at double speed dissolve into a ship's deck, and where Andrei Karpathi sits across from Odie with a *vibes* sticker on his laptop.

places.realPlace: Mount Circeo (Monte Circeo Promontory, Lazio, Italy) + Adaptive-Reuse Industrial Bottling Plant Loft

places.realPlace: IBM Poughkeepsie System/360 Mainframe Hall & Sitterson Hall (UNC Chapel Hill, NC)
places.fictionalPlace: Pylos (Court of Aged Nestor in The Odyssey Book 3)
places.description: An island of paper where Fred Brookes sits at a desk the size of an IBM System/360 mainframe with his two-column ledger of what management bought and what it cost.

places.realPlace: Sirenuse / Li Galli Archipelago (Amalfi Coast, Italy) + Linus Torvalds's Home Office in Portland, Oregon
places.fictionalPlace: Island of the Sirens (The Odyssey Book 12)
places.description: A calm, glassy sea echoing with 312 unread messages (*Quick sync? Can you weigh in? Looping you in*) where Linos Torwald sits on a rock in a cardigan offering a folding chair.

places.storyName: Bell Works Garden (Land of the Lotus-Eaters)
places.realPlace: Bell Labs Holmdel Complex (Eero Saarinen's 'Bell Works' in Holmdel, NJ) & Murray Hill Courtyard, NJ
places.fictionalPlace: Land of the Lotus-Eaters (Djerba / The Odyssey Book 9)
places.description: A brick-and-glass laboratory gone soft with ivy where nobody has a title or a 1-on-1, the fruit tastes like an endless afternoon, Claude Shanning unicycles and juggles, and Theseus the mouse runs his maze.

places.storyName: The Oracle (A Cave Lit by GPU Fans)
places.realPlace: Sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi (Mount Parnassus, Greece) + OpenAI / Safe Superintelligence Compute Cluster (San Francisco & Palo Alto, CA)
places.fictionalPlace: Delphic Oracle / Cave of the Pythia
places.description: A humming server cave lit by GPU fans where Ilya Sutskov leads a circle of hoodie-wearing researchers chanting 'Feel the AGI!' while every screen flashes: WHICH PART OF YOU IS THE PART THAT KNOWS?

places.fictionalPlace: Aeolia, Floating Island of Aeolus (Lipari, Aeolian Islands)

places.realPlace: Keen Technologies & id Software Lab (Dallas / Richardson, Texas)
places.fictionalPlace: Philoctetes' Coastal Cave on Lemnos / Hephaestus's Forge
places.description: A quiet shed on a cold coast with half-built hardware, an oscilloscope, one enormous whiteboard, Carmick's farewell letter taped to the wall, excellent coffee, and only one mug.

links.label: PCMag: John Carmack Leaves Meta for Keen Technologies

places.storyName: Hassaby's Charter Room at DeepMound (Calypso's Golden Cage)
places.realPlace: Google DeepMind HQ (Platform 37 / Pancras Square, King's Cross, London) & University College London (UCL)
places.fictionalPlace: Ogygia, Calypso's Golden Island (The Odyssey Book 5)
places.description: A golden room with a nymph's patience in its walls that opens only when Leverage >= 5. On the walls hang framed reminders of the cost: senior departures and investor share-price wobbles.

places.storyName: Knuthe's Cave ('On the Bottom of Things')
places.realPlace: Donald Knuth's Email-Free Study on the Stanford University Campus (Stanford, CA)
places.fictionalPlace: Subterranean Oracle Cave of Trophonius at Lebadea / Proteus's Sea Cave

places.description: An inland road running down to the Pacific where journeymen walk the Tour de France, shrine carpenters rebuild Ise every 20 years, Living National Treasures pass on shokunin mastery, and Mau Piailug reads the swells without instruments.

places.realPlace: Cyclopean Isles (Aci Trezza, Sicily, Italy) + Corporate Performance Calibration War-Room
places.description: Home to an enormous performance dashboard with a single glowing bar-chart eye that eats engineers whose mastery leaves no measurable trace.

places.storyName: The Underworld (A Conference Hotel After the Conference)
places.realPlace: Brutalist Atrium Hotel Lobby (e.g., Atlanta Marriott Marquis / Hyatt Regency) + Necromanteion of Acheron (Epirus, Greece)
places.fictionalPlace: Nekyia / Halls of Hades (The Odyssey Book 11)
places.description: Grey carpet, discarded lanyards, shades of old reorganisations murmuring about roadmaps around a poured-out lukewarm oat flat white, and Ajax standing silent with his tools.

places.storyName: Ithaca: The Parents' House, Hendry Works & Laertes's Orchard
places.realPlace: Maryville, Tennessee (1609 Scenic Drive / Blount County in the Foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains) + Island of Ithaca (Ionian Sea, Greece)
places.fictionalPlace: Laertes's Farm and Orchard on Ithaca (The Odyssey Book 24)
places.description: A semi-detached house on the edge of a small town with an orchard behind it too big for the garden, where Lars grafts four kinds of apple onto one trunk ('the committee') in golden late afternoon light.

propsAndMonsters.name: The Great Bow of Ithaca (The Production Billing Service & Retry Loop)
propsAndMonsters.realObject: Legacy Production Billing Microservice (Norway VAT, Québec Invoicing, Idempotent Retry Loop)
propsAndMonsters.fictionalCounterpart: Odysseus's Unstringable Palintonos Bow & Argos the Faithful Hound (The Odyssey Books 17 & 21)
propsAndMonsters.description: Goes down at 4 p.m. on Homecoming day. Chad's holistic prompt deletes Québec; Dougie reboots it with confidence; only Odie (if Craft >= 5) or Ines (if `passedOnCraft == true`) can string it. In the Argos ending (Beat 104), the retry loop is the old dog that still remembers its master.

propsAndMonsters.name: Laertes's Orchard Trees ('The Committee') & Grafting Knife
propsAndMonsters.realObject: Bramley Apple, Three Discovery Apples, Fruitless Pear, Grafting Knife, and 4-on-1 Grafted Apple Tree
propsAndMonsters.fictionalCounterpart: Laertes's Thirteen Pear, Ten Apple, and Forty Fig Trees (The Odyssey Book 24)
propsAndMonsters.description: In the ideal ending (*Laertes's Orchard*, Beat 100), Odie names his father's trees—especially the grafted tree with four apple varieties on one trunk that Lars calls 'the committee'—and pairs them with the VAT bug, the Québec refactor, and the retry loop, moving Lars's pride off the title and onto his son.
